page: Amazon Web Services c7g.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V1 model running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across standard compute tasks. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1532.58 and a multi-core score of 6111.85. Memory bandwidth is measured at 385.54 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 106.7 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, performance drops to weak or poor levels in specific workloads. The Passmark CPU encryption test registers in the bottom 10% with a score of 548.88, and LLM text generation for a 7B model is poor at 5.99 tokens per second. Bzip3 decompression and ray tracing benchmarks also fall into the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7g.xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for ARM-native applications without the overhead of hyperthreading. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local storage, requiring external network storage solutions, and limited cryptographic and vector instruction extensions. The instance is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and database operations, where it demonstrates average throughput, but it is not recommended for heavy cryptographic processing or large language model inference.
